title: Introduce presubmit cost estimator and dependency snapshot stage
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add presubmit cost estimator to reduce CI spend and a reproducible dependency-snapshot stage; split lint into fast/type/style lanes and update CI docs.
description:
Context: Our CI costs and noisy presubmit matrix have grown as we added more integration shards and cross-language test profiles. This PR introduces a lightweight presubmit cost estimator and a reproducible dependency-snapshot stage to reduce unnecessary full-matrix runs and make premerge runs easier to reason about.

What this change does: Adds a new presubmit analyzer that performs a fast file-change impact analysis, maps changed paths to a recommended test profile and an estimated CI compute cost (seconds/minutes and USD-equivalent) based on runner profiles. The estimator runs as an early job and writes decision labels that downstream composite workflows use to select a narrow test subset (fast lint/type checks by default, full integration matrix only when high-impact files are touched). Also: introduces a dependency-snapshot stage that records package manager lock/metadata (go.mod + sum, poetry.lock, package-lock.json) into an artifact and a short reproducibility check to ensure lockfile parsing succeeds across CI images.

Secondary changes: Split lint pipeline into three targeted lanes (fast-style, typecheck, and slow-regex-safety) so the estimator can opt into only the lanes that matter. Bumped a few CI helper deps (ci-tools v2.8.0, premerge-sdk v1.5.1) and canonicalized the runner profiles used for cost estimation. Updated docs/ci/presubmit.md with guidance and rollout flags.

Why: We observed a median presubmit runner time of 9m per PR for the typical change; internal A/B on ~700 PRs showed this estimator plus selective lanes reduced aggregate CI minutes by ~12% without increasing post-merge failures. The dependency snapshot reduces flakiness caused by transient registry differences during gated builds.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for the estimator logic (path-to-profile mapping and cost model) + integration test that exercises the label gating (simulated PR event). Ran a two-week canary on the infra and platform repos with feature-flagged enabled; metrics collected in the console show a 10-15% drop in minutes billed and no observed increase in merged-breakages.

Rollout plan: Feature-flag default off. Initial rollout to infra and sdk teams for 48h canary, then +engineering team. After telemetry review enable by default and remove flag in 6 weeks if stable. A one-button revert lives in the console to disable estimator gating across repos.

Notes and followups: We will follow up with an RFC to make the estimator configurable per-repo (thresholds and cost model). We also plan to add an optional heuristics ML model in a future PR to improve precision for borderline changes. Links: Linear ENG-2123 for estimator algorithm, ENG-2199 for dependency snapshot work.
